Adopt no new unobserved entrant, no parking-lot exit into this domain, and no entry by the observed distant bus, utility vehicles, work-zone cones or rear traffic. Nearby sedan and departing pedestrian are retained explicitly. Static sidewalk fixtures remain outside the modeled roadway boundary. These restrictions exclude other world conditions; they do not assert absence of traffic outside the domain.

Assume the individually visible silver sedan is approximately 4.8 m long and 1.85 m wide. Its apparent size, oblique front view, curb contact region and road perspective support a center near [18,5.8], not certified monocular depth. Estimate a continuous approximately straight paved patch between right curb y=-3.6 and left curb y=8, truncated at x=-3 and x=26. The right bicycle strip is pavement. The nearby rear portion is an extrapolation of the same continuous observed street surface under local straightness and ground-planarity assumptions. Current footprint and intended forward route lie within this patch. Pedestrian position uses the supplied front-left camera axes, approximate foot contact, the same local scale and ego-history compensation. Contact selection, body priors and planarity are falsifiable assumptions represented by finite model residuals and nonzero road uncertainty.

The curb-aligned silver sedan is conditionally parked for two seconds. Adopted mode is stationary. Reasonable adverse mode permits center displacement up to 0.3 m in each fixed axis and yaw deviation up to 0.03 rad from pi throughout the interval. The adverse rectangle encloses its entire body over those ranges. Larger motion or pull-out is excluded by this explicit short-term condition.

Across the actual 0.007605-second evidence age through reference and the future horizon, assume absolute speed at most 2.1 m/s. Adverse mode allows vx in [-0.6,0.6] and vy in [-1.45,2] m/s, also subject to the total speed bound, including stopping and turning back. Body yaw may change arbitrarily; a 0.5 m radial extent bounds every orientation of the declared 0.8 by 0.6 m body. Running or faster lane-directed return is excluded.

Allow vehicle CENTER x from -0.05 to 19 m, with unchanged lateral limits [-0.55,0.55]. concrete_repair_request: Repair the supplied object/time/constraint conflict using only the same actual images and trusted capture. Keep existing actor IDs; explain any evidence-supported new, absent or reidentified actor in confidence_note. Only evidence-supported environment estimates or physically achievable behavior/target/stop revisions are allowed. target_region is the permitted vehicle CENTER region: you may revise it within the original road to include the true initial center and an appropriate route, or revise a reasonable speed preference. Do not enlarge road to repair target_region, and do not delete genuine stop/yield requirements without image-supported justification. Do not move an obstacle, enlarge the road, shrink residuals, remove an observed threat or discard reasonable adverse modes merely to pass. A numerical or conservative-planner issue is not permission to change scene facts. Changes to actor position, dimensions, occupancy or residual need explicit actual-image evidence and a stated basis. Retain unknown or failure where support is unavailable. Use the CURRENT target capture scene, revision and time IDs; the previous response is immutable diagnostic context from an earlier trial.
